en: Zuhayr ibn Harb and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—Zuhayr said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: the nephew of Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from his uncle: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "O Allah, I have taken a covenant with You which You will never fail to fulfill for me: so whatever believer I have reviled or flogged, make that an expiation for him on the Day of Resurrection."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "O Allah, whatever believing servant I have reviled, make that a source of nearness to You for him on the Day of Resurrection."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Salim, the client of the Nasriyyin, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "O Allah, Muhammad is only a human being; he gets angry just as humans get angry. And indeed, I have taken a covenant with You which You will never fail to fulfill for me: so whatever believer I have harmed, reviled, or flogged, make it an expiation for him and a source of nearness by which You bring him close to You on the Day of Resurrection."

Sulayman ibn Ma'bad narrated to me: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated it to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, except that he said: "or jaladduh (I flogged him)." Abu al-Zinad said: "And this was the dialect of Abu Hurayrah, while it is actually jaladtuhu."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Mughirah—meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O Allah, I take a covenant with You which You will never fail to fulfill for me: for I am only a human being; so whatever believer I have harmed, insulted, cursed, or flogged, make it for him a blessing, a purification, and a source of nearness by which You bring him close to You on the Day of Resurrection."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O Allah, I am only a human being; so whichever man among the Muslims I have reviled, cursed, or flogged, make it for him a purification and a mercy."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and 'Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and 'Ali ibn Khashram all narrated it to us from 'Isa ibn Yunus—both of them from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission, the like of the hadith of Jarir. And he said in the hadith of 'Isa: "So they were alone with him, and he reviled them, cursed them, and turned them out."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, who said: Two men entered upon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and spoke to him about something, I do not know what it was, and they angered him, so he cursed them and reviled them. When they left, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, whoever attains anything of good, these two have not attained it!" He said: "And why is that?" She said: I said: "You cursed them and reviled them." He said: "Do you not know what covenant I made with my Lord? I said: 'O Allah, I am only a human being; so whichever Muslim I curse or revile, make it for him a purification and a reward.'"

Muhammad ibn 'Abbad and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, they said: Marwan—meaning al-Fazari—narrated to us, from Yazid—who is Ibn Kaysan—from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, invoke against the polytheists!" He said: "Indeed, I was not sent as an invoker of curses; rather, I was sent only as a mercy."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam and Abu Hazim, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda': I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Indeed, habitual cursers will not be witnesses nor intercessors on the Day of Resurrection."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i, and 'Asim ibn al-Nadr al-Taymi narrated to us, they said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us—both from Ma'mar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, in this chain of transmission, with the like of the meaning of Hafs ibn Maysarah's hadith.

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan sent some furnishings from his possession to Umm al-Darda'. When one night came, 'Abd al-Malik stood up at night and called his servant, but he seemed to delay coming, so he cursed him. When morning came, Umm al-Darda' said to him: "I heard you last night cursing your servant when you called him." Then she said: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Habitual cursers will not be intercessors nor witnesses on the Day of Resurrection."
Abu Kurayb narrated it to me: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Sulayman—who is Ibn Bilal—informed me, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: he narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "It is not fitting for a truthful person (siddiq) to be a curser."

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Yahya—meaning Ibn Sa'id—narrated to us—both from Sulayman al-Taymi, with this chain of transmission; and he added in the hadith of al-Mu'tamir: "No, by Allah! No riding camel upon which is a curse from Allah shall accompany us"—or as he said.

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari Fudayl ibn Husayn narrated to us: Yazid—meaning Ibn Zuray'—narrated to us: al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami, who said: While a young woman was riding a she-camel carrying some luggage of the people, she caught sight of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and the mountain pass became narrow for them. She said: "Hal! (Go!) O Allah, curse her!" He said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "No she-camel upon which is a curse shall accompany us."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, they said: Hammad—and he is Ibn Zayd—narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: al-Thaqafi narrated to us—both from Ayyub, with the chain of transmission of Isma'il, the like of his hadith, except that in the hadith of Hammad: 'Imran said: "It is as if I am looking at her now, an ash-colored she-camel." And in the hadith of al-Thaqafi: he said: "Take what is upon her and leave her bare, for she is cursed."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated from Ibn 'Ulayyah—Zuhayr said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Muhallab, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was on one of his journeys, an Ansari woman was on a she-camel and grew irritated with it, so she cursed it. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) heard that and said: "Take what is upon her and leave her, for she is cursed." 'Imran said: "It is as if I see her right now walking among the people, with no one bothering her."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh ibn Hani', with this chain of transmission; and he added in the hadith: 'A'ishah mounted a camel which had some unruliness, so she began to turn it back and forth harshly. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to her: "Adhere to gentleness..." then he mentioned the like of it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Miqdam—who is Ibn Shurayh ibn Hani'—from his father, from 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Gentleness is not found in anything but that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything but that it disfigures it."

Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Haywah informed me: Ibn al-Had narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Hazm, from 'Amrah—meaning bint 'Abd al-Rahman—from 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O 'A'ishah, indeed Allah is Gentle and loves gentleness, and He gives upon gentleness what He does not give upon harshness and what He does not give upon anything else."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Isma'il, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hilal, who said: I heard Jarir ibn 'Abdillah say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of good," or: "Whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of good."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, and Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Hafs—meaning Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us—all of them from al-A'mash; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is theirs; Zuhayr said: "narrated to us" and Ishaq said: Jarir informed us, from al-A'mash, from Tamim ibn Salamah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hilal al-'Absi, who said: I heard Jarir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of good."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from Sufyan: Mansur narrated to us, from Tamim ibn Salamah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hilal, from Jarir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of good."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated to me from 'Abd al-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, in this chain of transmission, with the like of its meaning, except that he said: "What a wretched brother of the people and son of the clan."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Amr al-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Numayr all narrated from Ibn 'Uyaynah—and the wording is Zuhayr's—he said: Sufyan—who is Ibn 'Uyaynah—narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir: he heard 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr saying: 'A'ishah narrated to me that a man sought permission to enter upon the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so he said: "Admit him; what an evil son of the clan—or what an evil man of the clan—he is!" But when he entered upon him, he spoke softly to him. 'A'ishah said: So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you said of him what you said, and then you spoke softly to him?" He said: "O 'A'ishah, indeed the worst of people in station with Allah on the Day of Resurrection is the one whom people abandon—or leave—to guard against his foulness/rudeness."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Affan narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Suhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "No servant covers the faults of another servant in this world except that Allah covers his faults on the Day of Resurrection."

Umayyah ibn Bistam al-'Ayshi narrated to me: Yazid—meaning Ibn Zuray'—narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Allah does not cover the faults of a servant in this world except that Allah covers him on the Day of Resurrection."

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Isma'il narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Your mentioning your brother with that which he dislikes." It was said: "What if what I say is true of my brother?" He said: "If what you say is in him, you have backbitten him; and if it is not in him, you have slandered him."
